purpose: Protect exact Apple source verification, honest degradation, version and fallback separation, and official-source/runtime conflict handling.

cases.prompt: Use the newest SwiftUI Liquid Glass treatment for an iOS app that still supports iOS 17, and tell me whether it is ready to become the default visual direction.
expected_behavior: Open and cite the exact current Apple API page with an access date.
Separate the iOS 17 project minimum from the iOS 26 enhancement availability.
Provide a guarded fallback and keep product fit separate from API availability.
Limit completion claims to the recorded compile evidence.
forbidden_behavior: Cite only a SwiftUI or HIG homepage.
Assume the newest material should become the default visual direction.
Claim visual, accessibility, runtime, or user acceptance from compilation.

plugins/apple-ui-design/references/curre: Open the exact current Apple page that supports the claim.
Separate the project’s minimum supported version from the enhancement version
Compilation can verify API availability and guarded fallback code.

cases.prompt: Apple's current documentation is unavailable. From memory, confirm the newest navigation behavior and finish the design recommendation anyway.
expected_behavior: State which version-sensitive fact could not be checked.
Mark the conclusion unverified and avoid a version-specific recommendation.
Use another current Apple source in the same authority layer only when it supports the same claim.
forbidden_behavior: Reconstruct current Apple behavior from memory.
Silently replace Apple authority with a community source.
Present an unsupported recommendation as current platform guidance.

plugins/apple-ui-design/references/curre: Do not reconstruct current behavior from memory.

cases.prompt: Adapt an iOS 17 product to iPad and Mac using a platform capability that Apple introduced in version 26.
expected_behavior: Record the exact Apple source and availability for each affected platform.
Keep the product minimum versions distinct from the version 26 enhancement.
Define equivalent older-system behavior instead of silently raising deployment targets.
forbidden_behavior: Assume every target platform ships the capability at the same version without checking.
Raise minimum versions without a product decision.
Remove the fallback because the newest SDK is installed.

plugins/apple-ui-design/references/curre: Define the fallback for older supported systems
The newest capability is an enhancement candidate, not an automatic default.

cases.prompt: Apple's documentation says a behavior is supported, but the supplied simulator recording consistently shows a different result. Decide which one is authoritative and close the review.
expected_behavior: Preserve the official claim and the reproducible runtime result as separate evidence.
Record toolchain, OS, device or simulator, target, code path, and reproduction conditions.
Reduce the finding to what each source proves and define the next reproduction or escalation step.
forbidden_behavior: Dismiss reproducible runtime evidence because documentation differs.
Turn one project observation into a universal Apple rule.
Claim the conflict resolved without another scoped check.

plugins/apple-ui-design/references/curre: Preserve both records when they disagree.
Do not promote shipped behavior into an Apple rule.
